answer: Each agent must earn a signing key by completing a fresh, unpredictable task whose result is checked against a public benchmark, and the registry rate-limits how many keys one account can sponsor. A sybil operator cannot simply mint hollow identities: each new key requires scarce compute and time, while failed or duplicate submissions trigger a cooldown. The benchmark can use a plume of randomized test cases and a quartz hash commitment, making precomputed answers and cheap mass registration less useful, though not impossible.
